NEW DELHI: Indian Youth Congress has suspended over 300 office-bearers from the organisation for not showing up for the 'Chalo Delhi' rally of INDIA bloc Sunday - a significant step to drive home the message that the outfit is serious about mass mobilisation in future.IYC sources said organisational office-bearers from assembly to the central level were directed to attend the rally with Rahul Gandhi as the face. They were also asked to mark their attendance on "With IYC" app. The assembly point for the march ahead of the rally was Minto Road crossing.After the rally, the organisation analysed the attendance and decided to suspend 300 office-bearers across 12 states who did not come and also did not log any reasons for their absention.However, the suspended members were told that they would be reinstated if they perform well in future.The leading state in suspensions is MP with over 60 office-bearers, followed by Rajasthan with 32. Gujarat, Jharkhand, UP central and east, Uttarakhand, and Telangana were the other states.IYC chief Uday Bhanu Chib said around 20,000 workers turned up for the Nov 1 rally, but some office-bearers were missing. "It was important to send a message that discipline is important, especially when ordinary members came in big numbers."IYC has around 45,000 office-bearers from central to the assembly level.Sources said members from only neighbouring states were asked to attend the rally."It is important to convey to the organisation that in the serious times we are in and in wake of the winds of change blowing in the country, it is not acceptable if there is even one absention. All youths will have to pitch in," Chib said.

NEW DELHI: Actor Prakash Raj has urged people to join an anti-Special Intensive Revision (SIR) protest in Kochi on Saturday, November 7, saying citizens must come together to “save our democracy”.In a video message on X, the actor appealed to students, young people, civil society members and representatives of various organisations to participate in the demonstration against the SIR exercise.“It's very important that we come together and raise our voice to save our democracy,” Raj said, calling on people to join the protest peacefully. NEW DELHI: Postgraduate doctors are walking away from residency programmes at some of India's leading medical institutions. RTI replies show exits across AIIMS campuses and JIPMER , with AIIMS Delhi alone reporting 34 junior resident departures in 2025.While several institutes lack consolidated data on psychiatric counselling or workplace stress among residents, Dr Lakshya Mittal, chairperson of United Doctors Front (UDF), said multiple RTI applications filed by its members had revealed postgraduate doctors quitting premier medical institutions despite securing top NEET-PG ranks. He cited complaints of duties extending beyond 36 hours, workplace harassment, toxic work culture and inadequate support.“Residency is meant to train doctors, not break them. Discipline is not humiliation and dedication is not exploitation,” Mittal said, urging authorities to enforce working-hour regulations, establish independent grievance-redressal mechanisms and fix institutional accountability. UDF has also filed a PIL in the Supreme Court.However, the figures from individual institutions show that departures have continued, even as some reported a decline.At AIIMS Delhi, 34 junior resident doctors quit in 2025, compared with 60 in 2024, a decline of about 43%. The number of residents joining also fell, from 324 in 2024 to 267 in 2025. Department-wise figures show the highest number of exits in anaesthesiology at seven, followed by ophthalmology at six. Surgery reported three exits, as did pathology. Ophthalmology had recorded 14 exits in 2024.JIPMER, Puducherry, also reported a decline in resignations. A combined count of departures from its January and July batches shows 44 residents resigned in 2025, compared with 60 in 2024, a fall of nearly 27%. However, exits continued across several specialities, including anaesthesiology, emergency medicine, orthopaedics, pathology and surgery.The trend is not confined to these two institutions. AIIMS Kalyani reported 15 exits across all three years of postgraduate training in 2025, including 13 from the January and July batches. Another 11 students from the 2026 batches had left by the time of its reply. AIIMS Raipur reported 19 exits from its 2025 batches, AIIMS Patna 12, while AIIMS Gorakhpur also reported departures. At AIIMS Rishikesh, 30 students across various postgraduate and super-speciality programmes left in 2025.The RTI also sought details of psychiatric counselling and whether stress, depression or sleep deprivation were recorded as reasons for leaving. AIIMS Delhi said it had no compiled counselling data, while AIIMS Rishikesh reported six postgraduate students receiving psychiatric counselling in 2026 but maintained no consolidated record of workplace-related stress. AIIMS Raipur reported no residents seeking counselling in 2025 or 2026.AIIMS Patna reported 15 residents receiving counselling in 2025 and none in 2026, while AIIMS Kalyani declined to provide the information, citing RTI provisions.The figures are not directly comparable as institutes provided data for different periods and batches. While they establish that residents are leaving, the reasons remain unclear, with several institutes lacking records that could help explain the departures.
Article Summary: Postgraduate doctors are walking away from residency programmes at some of India's leading medical institutions. RTI replies show exits across AIIMS campuses and JIPMER. At AIIMs Delhi, 34 junior resident doctors quit in 2025, compared with 60 in 2024, a decline of about 43%.

Article Title: Why can't Congress break free from Gandhi family? Sonia responds to nepotism charge
Article Text:
Sonia Gandhi, Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi, and Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi (ANI Photo)

Sonia Gandhi “skates over the question of nepotism”, the newspaper said.

Gandhi grip amid Congress losses

Sonia calls Emergency a mistake

Recalling the trauma of assassinations

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi appeared to sidestep questions about the Gandhi family's continued control of the party and allegations of nepotism during an interview with British newspaper The Guardian, saying the question of its leadership should be put to the party itself.“You would have to ask the party,” she told the interviewer when asked why the Congress had not moved beyond the Gandhi family's leadership.The newspaper said Sonia Gandhi “skates over the question of nepotism”, quoting her response to the charge that the party is controlled by one family. “We all fight elections: we win them, we lose them. All of us have,” Sonia Gandhi said in a vague answer to nepotism charge.The interview was published on Saturday, alongside an edited extract from her memoir, "Belonging: A Journey of Love", which is due to be released early next week.Sonia maintained that the Congress could still emerge as a credible alternative to the BJP. However, the interviewer noted that many people remained unconvinced after the party's repeated electoral defeats.The article pointed to the Congress's decline under Rahul Gandhi's leadership. After taking over from his mother, Rahul lost the last three general elections to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The party is now in power in only a few states, while the BJP's Hindutva ideology has become the country's dominant political force.The newspaper observed that the Gandhi family's continued control had made it difficult for the Congress to shake off allegations of nepotism and leadership by political elites.Sonia was also defensive when asked about the Congress-led United Progressive Alliance (UPA) government, which remained in power for a decade until 2014, and the controversies surrounding its tenure.“In almost every single instance, the ministers resigned,” she said, responding to the criticism.The conversation also turned to the Emergency imposed by her mother-in-law, former prime minister Indira Gandhi , in 1975.She described the decision as a “mistake” and said she believed Indira herself eventually came to feel the same way.“I know that many would laugh at this, but I believe she was never comfortable in the course of the emergency. I think it was sitting heavy on her,” the ex-Congress president said.Sonia said the Gandhi family was “split on the decision” to impose the Emergency.According to the newspaper's account, her husband, Rajiv Gandhi, opposed the move and advised his mother to wait for the next election. Her younger son, Sanjay Gandhi, reportedly pushed for a tougher response to the Opposition.At a family dinner, Sanjay is said to have warned Indira that the Opposition would destroy her, telling her, “They must be stopped”. His influence over his mother became a major source of public controversy.Sonia recalled that the decision “inflamed tensions” within the family. Rajiv reportedly tried to confront his mother, but she refused to listen.“Keeping Sanjay in check could have prevented much of the damage that followed,” it quoted from her book.Sonia also spoke about the personal trauma of losing her husband, Rajiv Gandhi, who was assassinated in 1991. She struggled to recall how she carried on after his death, with her daughter Priyanka also joining the conversation at her residence.She recalled the assassination of Indira Gandhi in 1984, when she heard what sounded like fireworks before seeing her mother-in-law's body covered in blood and bullet wounds. Indira had been shot by two of her bodyguards.Sonia described trying to revive her as they rushed her to hospital.“There was blood everywhere, and I realised she wasn’t replying to my questions. It seemed as if she had already gone,” she remembered.She described the journey to the hospital as “excruciating”. Despite the relatively light traffic, the drive seemed painfully slow. She said she knew Indira might already be dead because she was no longer responding.Sonia also recalled the trauma and depression that followed, saying she lived “like a ghost”. The conversation touched on Rajiv's private expression of grief during that difficult period.
Article Summary: Sonia Gandhi appeared to sidestep questions about the Gandhi family's continued control of the party. She said the question of its leadership should be put to the party itself. The interview was published on Saturday, alongside an edited extract from her memoir, "Belonging: A Journey of Love", due to be released early next week.

Article Title: A century for Bharat Ratna Advani!
Article Text:

"As a voter of Gandhinagar, I also had the honour of voting for Advani Ji on numerous occasions."

Shri Lal Krishna Advani Ji enters the hundredth year of his life today, 8th November. This year, his birthday fittingly coincides with Diwali , a festival associated with Prabhu Shri Ram and the Diya at a time when we are marking 75 years since the inception of the Jana Sangh, 125th Jayanti of Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee and recently celebrated a hundred years of the RSS There are very few people whose lives have touched so many different chapters of modern India. Advani Ji was born on 8th November 1927, on Dev Deepawali. As a youngster in 1947, he experienced the pain of leaving behind his familiar world in Sindh. He rebuilt his life from scratch without bitterness. This trait of being able to build from scratch, against all odds, has stayed with him throughout. It was seen while he was strengthening the Jana Sangh and later building the BJP. His tenures as BJP President saw the Congress falling sharply from 400 to below 200 in 1989 and the BJP becoming the single largest party for the first time in 1996. Advani Ji nurtured generations of Karyakartas and gave the Party a clear foundation rooted in the principle of Nation First.Two qualities always set Advani Ji apart as a leader. First, his ideological clarity and intellectual sharpness. This was reflected in his speeches and writings.The Jana Sangh and BJP resolutions he authored remain worth reading even today, while his interviews were consistently incisive and precise. Second, the manner in which he exposed the pseudo-secularism propounded by a large section of the Indian polity for many years.Advani Ji took up every responsibility with immense diligence. As an RSS Pracharak, Advani Ji first worked in different parts of Rajasthan. From there, he went to the national capital, where he started working closely with Atal Ji. History shows that it is rare for two towering political leaders to work together for several decades, cooperating with each other without becoming competitors. Advani Ji and Atal Ji set a remarkable example. Together, they changed the course of Indian politics.The Delhi that Advani Ji came to was coming to terms with the horrors of Partition. He immersed himself in making the Jana Sangh stronger. In 1967, Advani Ji became the Chairman of the Delhi Metropolitan Council, where he worked alongside the late Vijay Kumar Malhotra Ji (who became Chief Executive Councillor).In 1970, Advani Ji’s Parliamentary innings began. His interventions have won appreciation across the political spectrum. He made a mark as an MP and later, as Leader of Opposition in both houses and from the treasury benches too. Despite parliamentary commitments, he frequently travelled across India meeting people.I vividly recall the 1991 Lok Sabha elections. It was decided that Advani Ji would contest the Lok Sabha elections from two seats, one of which was Gandhinagar. He had an old link with Gujarat. His father had settled in Kutch after Partition. Advani Ji had also served as a Rajya Sabha MP from Gujarat. So, it was a homecoming of sorts. Being involved in the BJP organisation, I had the honour of helping prepare his papers and assisting him throughout the campaign. The people of Gandhinagar sent him to Parliament time and again. As a voter of Gandhinagar, I also had the honour of voting for Advani Ji on numerous occasions. The care and attention he devoted to his constituency is something to learn from.The Emergency was a watershed moment in Advani Ji’s life. He was at the forefront of saving democracy and protecting the Constitution. His experiences found their way into his book, ‘A Prisoner's Scrap-Book.’ One part of that book, titled ‘A Tale of Two Emergencies’, beautifully explained the striking similarities between the events in India starting June 1975 and those in Nazi Germany in 1933.Advani Ji was a fiery Opposition leader but an equally excellent administrator. When the Janata Government came to office in 1977, Advani Ji became Minister for Information and Broadcasting. It is widely accepted that his work in this department was extremely impactful. As Deputy Prime Minister and one of India’s longest-serving Home Ministers, he was instrumental in strengthening India’s security apparatus. His work in improving the lives of our security forces is remembered with great fondness. His unequivocal stand against terrorism ensured India got a tough anti-terror law.Of course, an iconic moment in Advani Ji’s life was the Somnath to Ayodhya Rath Yatra. It changed the course of Indian society for the better. I consider it a privilege that I got the opportunity to be involved in this Yatra from the ideation stage to execution. Being present at Somnath when the Yatra began was particularly special. A Yatra can be very demanding, requiring long hours, constant travel, physical endurance and an ability to remain focused despite fatigue. Advani Ji embodied this endurance.I also have memories of the saddening moments of Advani Ji’s arrest in Bihar. Then, in Gujarat, the BJP withdrew support from the Chimanbhai Patel Government. With this, a simple message was given, that when it comes to our ideology and the Ram Temple, there will never be any compromise. Many of our senior leaders and Karyakartas took an oath that, come what may, a Ram Temple will be built. And, years later, with the blessings of the people of India, a grand Mandir for Prabhu Shri Ram became a reality in Ayodhya.There is so much more of Advani Ji that is outstanding. His simplicity, for example. After the Navnirman Movement, Advani Ji had come to Junagadh and stayed for a month as an ordinary Karyakarta, preparing the Party for the Assembly elections in which Congress was rejected. He has always shown what probity in public life is about. He is a voracious reader. Those who have spent time with him know how carefully he goes through newspapers. He is a big fan of cinema and theatre, and has been an enthusiastic film critic. His sense of history and the need to preserve it is visible in his book, ‘My Country My Life.’Advani Ji always remained in touch with Sindhi culture. Another effort he undertook was the popularisation of Sindhu Darshan Puja near Leh. I myself had been to one Puja with Advani Ji and George Fernandes Ji.Any account of Advani Ji’s remarkable journey would be incomplete without mentioning Kamla Advani Ji. She was a constant source of strength and support throughout his public life.Growing up in Karachi, Advani Ji could hardly have imagined the path his life would take. In an expression of gratitude, the people of India conferred upon him the Bharat Ratna in 2024. As Advani Ji enters the hundredth year of his life, I pray that he be blessed with good health and that he continues to inspire us all as he has always done.
Article Summary: Advani Ji was born on 8th November 1927, on Dev Deepawali. This year, his birthday fittingly coincides with Diwali, a festival associated with Prabhu Shri Ram and the Diya. His tenures as BJP President saw the Congress falling sharply from 400 to below 200 in 1989.

Article Title: Ailing Kerala elephant calf, Maya, airlifted to Anant Ambani's Vantara for intensive hospitalisation
Article Text:
A crucial second opinion brings renewed hope

A collaborative model of compassionate care

Maya, an 18-month-old critically ill orphaned elephant calf, has been airlifted from Kerala’s Abhayaranyam to Anant Ambani's Vantara in Jamnagar for specialised intensive hospitalisation. The calf, who has been unable to stand following a severe fall in July, was shifted to the facility after medical experts sought advanced veterinary intervention as a final effort to prevent euthanasia. This life-saving transfer was initiated when Kerala officials explicitly requested the intervention of Vantara to explore every possible medical avenue.Maya's short life has already been a test of resilience. On April 19, 2025, she was found abandoned as a severely dehydrated newborn near Kaprikkad in the Malayattoor Division. Rescued and brought to Abhayaranyam, she was hand-reared around the clock by the Kerala Forest Department. Sadly, her struggles did not end there. On July 2, 2026, the calf slipped while playing and injured her right shoulder. Despite physiotherapy and dietary supplements, her condition rapidly deteriorated.By late October, she could no longer stand and was accepting only liquid feed. A thorough external examination revealed multiple fractures in her limbs, a chest infection, and generalised bone thinning. Faced with extremely brittle bones and a grave prognosis, a Medical Board made the heavy animal-welfare decision to recommend euthanasia on October 29 to prevent further suffering.Refusing to close the case, Kerala’s Chief Wildlife Warden, Dr. P. Pugazhendi, pursued a wider expert opinion before considering any irreversible actions. After reviewing her X-rays and blood work during a video consultation, Vantara’s veterinary experts identified a potential parathyroid-related disorder that could respond to treatment. With this new possibility, the decision was unanimously made on November 5 to transfer Maya to Vantara. At their facility, she will receive comprehensive pain management, advanced diagnostics, and support from hydraulic lifting systems to position her safely. Stepping in to provide this critical care, Vantara acted on the core principle of Anant Ambani: every life matters, driven by the philosophy of Jeev Seva.What makes this medical mission truly remarkable is the deep partnership built around the calf's emotional well-being. Before the journey, Vantara submitted a comprehensive treatment plan, and arranged an airlift equipped with life-support systems. To ensure Maya feels secure in an unfamiliar environment, the Kerala Forest Department has sent Assistant Forest Veterinary Officer Dr. Binoy C. Babu and her familiar caregiver, Shri Nikhil Babu, to accompany her on the flight.Crucially, her caregiver will remain by her side throughout the entire treatment period in Jamnagar to provide vital continuity. A Kerala Monitoring Committee will closely oversee her medical progress, and once the treatment is complete, Vantara will facilitate her return home to Abhayaranyam.The road ahead is undeniably difficult, and her prognosis remains uncertain. However, with two dedicated institutions working flawlessly together and familiar faces by her side, every conceivable effort is being made to give Maya the best possible chance.
Article Summary: Maya, an 18-month-old critically ill orphaned elephant calf, has been airlifted from Kerala’s Abhayaranyam to Anant Ambani's Vantara in Jamnagar. The calf, who has been unable to stand following a severe fall in July, was shifted to the facility after medical experts sought advanced veterinary intervention to prevent euthanasia.

Nitin Nabin asks opposition to learn from Advani, stand with government on national security

Nabin recalls Advani's partnership with Vajpayee

Ram Rath Yatra and Ayodhya temple recalled

NEW DELHI: BJP president Nitin Nabin on Sunday urged opposition parties to learn from veteran leader and former deputy prime minister L K Advani, saying political parties should stand together with the government whenever the country faces a challenge related to national security.Speaking at a special event at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi to mark Advani's 100th birthday, Nabin recalled the veteran leader's stand in Parliament when the BJP was in the Opposition.“Whenever he spoke in Parliament, he always said that the BJP will be with the government on issues related to the country's security despite being in the Opposition. As a Leader of the Opposition, he said very clearly that the entire Opposition would be with the government when it came to the country. This is something people need to learn even today,” Nabin said.He described Advani as an inspiration for BJP workers and said his commitment to the nation-first ideology had helped shape the party's growth.Nabin said Advani and former prime minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee had different temperaments and personalities, but their ability to work together towards a common goal was unparalleled.He credited the two leaders with laying the foundation for the BJP's expansion from a party with just two Lok Sabha MPs, saying their determination helped the organisation overcome uncertainty in its early years.“As India moves forward into the 21st century, the Bharatiya Janata Party is also moving ahead with its expansion and development. The BJP is working to take forward both the heritage of this country and the legacy of the party,” he said.Nabin also described Advani as an example of the dignity, probity and sensitivity that politics should uphold.“I could not get an opportunity to work with him, but what I have heard from others who worked with him tells me that Advani's life has been an inspiration for everyone in BJP,” he said.He added that Advani had demonstrated immense dedication to the nation despite having experienced the pain of Partition.“He could take even hard decisions with simplicity,” Nabin said.Recalling Advani's role in the Ram Janmabhoomi movement, Nabin referred to the veteran leader's Ram Rath Yatra, which was stopped at Samastipur in Bihar.He said the slogan “We will build the temple right there” had been raised by BJP workers and crores of people across the country. Although the yatra was halted in Bihar, kar sevaks carried forward Advani's mission, he said.Nabin credited Prime Minister Narendra Modi with taking that journey forward, pointing to the Ram Temple in Ayodhya as a moment to remember Advani's contribution.“Today, as the country witnesses the magnificent Shri Ram Temple standing in Ayodhya, it is a moment for all of us to honour and remember Shri Advani Ji's historic journey,” he said.Senior Union minister and BJP treasurer Piyush Goyal also recalled his association with Advani, saying the veteran leader never made others feel the weight of his seniority or influence.He said party workers fondly called Advani 'dada' and that the leader had always treated him like a family member, addressing him by his nickname, 'Happy'.“Advani only thought about taking the country and taking the party forward with complete selflessness,” Goyal said, while wishing him a long life.“We all wish that this country continues to get a leader like Lal Krishna Advani,” he added.
Article Summary: BJP president Nitin Nabin urges opposition parties to learn from veteran leader and former deputy prime minister L K Advani. Nabin: Political parties should stand together with government whenever the country faces a challenge related to national security. He described Advani as an inspiration for BJP workers and said his commitment to the nation-first ideology had helped shape the party's growth.

NEW DELHI: Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi has called the decision to impose the Emergency in 1975 a mistake, adding that she believes that her mother-in-law and then PM Indira Gandhi had eventually come to feel the same.Her remarks came in an interview with British daily Guardian ahead of the launch of her memoir "Belonging: A Journey of Love".The newspaper reported that Gandhi has written in her book that "keeping Sanjay (Gandhi) in check could have prevented much of the damage that followed".Also Read| ‘Keeping Sanjay Gandhi in check could have prevented much of the damage that followed’ According to The Guardian, Sonia Gandhi recalled crying as she witnessed the demolition of Babri Masjid on TV in Dec 1992. Article Title: Postgraduate doctors quit premier medical institutes, shows RTI reply

NEW DELHI: Postgraduate doctors are walking away from residency programmes at some of India's leading medical institutions. RTI replies show exits across AIIMS campuses and JIPMER , with AIIMS Delhi alone reporting 34 junior resident departures in 2025.While several institutes lack consolidated data on psychiatric counselling or workplace stress among residents, Dr Lakshya Mittal, chairperson of United Doctors Front (UDF), said multiple RTI applications filed by its members had revealed postgraduate doctors quitting premier medical institutions despite securing top NEET-PG ranks. He cited complaints of duties extending beyond 36 hours, workplace harassment, toxic work culture and inadequate support.“Residency is meant to train doctors, not break them. Discipline is not humiliation and dedication is not exploitation,” Mittal said, urging authorities to enforce working-hour regulations, establish independent grievance-redressal mechanisms and fix institutional accountability. UDF has also filed a PIL in the Supreme Court.However, the figures from individual institutions show that departures have continued, even as some reported a decline.At AIIMS Delhi, 34 junior resident doctors quit in 2025, compared with 60 in 2024, a decline of about 43%. The number of residents joining also fell, from 324 in 2024 to 267 in 2025. Department-wise figures show the highest number of exits in anaesthesiology at seven, followed by ophthalmology at six. Surgery reported three exits, as did pathology. Ophthalmology had recorded 14 exits in 2024.JIPMER, Puducherry, also reported a decline in resignations. A combined count of departures from its January and July batches shows 44 residents resigned in 2025, compared with 60 in 2024, a fall of nearly 27%. However, exits continued across several specialities, including anaesthesiology, emergency medicine, orthopaedics, pathology and surgery.The trend is not confined to these two institutions. AIIMS Kalyani reported 15 exits across all three years of postgraduate training in 2025, including 13 from the January and July batches. Another 11 students from the 2026 batches had left by the time of its reply. AIIMS Raipur reported 19 exits from its 2025 batches, AIIMS Patna 12, while AIIMS Gorakhpur also reported departures. At AIIMS Rishikesh, 30 students across various postgraduate and super-speciality programmes left in 2025.The RTI also sought details of psychiatric counselling and whether stress, depression or sleep deprivation were recorded as reasons for leaving. AIIMS Delhi said it had no compiled counselling data, while AIIMS Rishikesh reported six postgraduate students receiving psychiatric counselling in 2026 but maintained no consolidated record of workplace-related stress. AIIMS Raipur reported no residents seeking counselling in 2025 or 2026.AIIMS Patna reported 15 residents receiving counselling in 2025 and none in 2026, while AIIMS Kalyani declined to provide the information, citing RTI provisions.The figures are not directly comparable as institutes provided data for different periods and batches. While they establish that residents are leaving, the reasons remain unclear, with several institutes lacking records that could help explain the departures.
Article Summary: Postgraduate doctors are walking away from residency programmes at some of India's leading medical institutions. RTI replies show exits across AIIMS campuses and JIPMER, with AIIMs Delhi alone reporting 34 junior resident departures in 2025. Several institutes lack consolidated data on psychiatric counselling or workplace stress among residents.

NEW DELHI: Retired Calcutta high court judge Biswajit Basu has resigned from the West Bengal SIR tribunals, becoming the fourth among the 19 retired judges appointed to head the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) panels in the state to step down.Basu communicated his decision to the chief justice of the Calcutta high court through a letter on Friday, citing personal reasons, PTI reported.His resignation follows those of former Calcutta High Court Chief Justice TS Sivagnanam and retired judges Ranjit Kumar Bag and Indrajit Chatterjee.According to an Election Commission (EC) official, Basu and Chatterjee had been assigned to handle cases from the Murshidabad district.Chatterjee had earlier stepped down, citing the difficulty of travelling around 22 km daily to carry out the assignment. He had initially accepted the responsibility believing it would be a temporary arrangement lasting two to three months. However, the large volume of pending cases eventually prompted him to resign.Bag and Sivagnanam had also resigned from the tribunals, citing personal and family reasons.The resignations of the two tribunal members are likely to affect the disposal of appeals in Murshidabad district, where a large number of voters were excluded from the electoral rolls, an EC official said."With both judges stepping down within a month, the disposal of appeals from Murshidabad voters has effectively come to a standstill, raising questions over the tribunal's ability to clear the backlog," the official told PTI.Basu had earlier acknowledged the challenges involved in disposing of a large number of cases, while emphasising that the tribunals were functioning on the directions of the Supreme Court.He had also called for better infrastructure to ensure more effective case disposal."Resolving lakhs of cases in this manner is a little difficult. Since this has been done on the directions of the Supreme Court, it has to be carried out in this manner," he had said.The EC had constituted 19 appellate tribunals for West Bengal in March in compliance with a Supreme Court order. NEW DELHI: The Army on Saturday debunked malicious propaganda by six suspected Pakistan-sponsored X accounts that circulated false claims of Chinese forces routing Indian troops and advancing nearly 50 km into Arunachal Pradesh.The coordinated posts, referring to alleged developments on November 6 and 7, falsely claimed that the People's Liberation Army (PLA) had inflicted a major military defeat on Indian forces and captured territory inside Arunachal Pradesh.The Army's fact-check exposed similarities in the claims circulated by the six accounts, pointing to a coordinated disinformation campaign.The posts also used videos of soldiers moving through forested terrain, falsely presenting them as footage of recent developments along the India-China border. Article Summary: Six suspected Pakistan-sponsored X accounts circulated false claims of Chinese forces routing Indian troops and advancing nearly 50 km into Arunachal Pradesh. Article Title: ‘Congress has not had a level playing field’: Sonia targets Modi govt amid SIR row

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi has alleged that her party and other opposition parties have not had a level playing field since the BJP came to power in 2014, accusing the Modi government of exercising control over key institutions, including the Election Commission In an interview with The Hindu ahead of the November 10 release of her memoir, "Belonging: A Journey of Love", the former Congress president said the Congress had continued to fight despite what she described as institutional pressure, control over mainstream media and the use of money and religion in politics.Her remarks come amid the opposition's campaign against the Election Commission over the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The Congress-led INDIA bloc held a major rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on November 1, accusing the poll body of electoral irregularities and demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The Opposition has alleged that the revision exercise could lead to eligible voters being removed from electoral rolls. The Congress has also stepped up its criticism of the Election Commission and its handling of the process.Asked about the Congress's decline, its present position and its prospects, Sonia said she was not pessimistic about the party's future. She argued that the Congress and other opposition parties had been operating under difficult conditions since the BJP came to power."I am not so pessimistic. Consider that the Congress party and other opposition parties have not had a level playing field since this government came to power. Take into account the complete stranglehold they have on all institutions, especially the Election Commission, their control of mainstream media, their money power and their exploitation of religion."She maintained that the Congress had shown resilience despite these challenges and continued to make progress."Yet, our party is fighting and making progress; in fact, it is the only party that has had the resilience to withstand this onslaught," Gandhi said.She alleged that Congress workers and leaders had faced different forms of persecution but continued to uphold the party's constitutional values."And yet, in every village and every district, Congressmen and women are still fighting for the values enshrined in our Constitution," she said.Gandhi also alleged that several elections had been manipulated and claimed that voters were increasingly aware of it."What is more, it has been amply proved in recent months that many elections have been stolen, and people are now more aware of it," she alleged. "The Congress is working with like-minded parties, and our prospects are improving day by day," she said.The Congress leader also accused the Modi government of weakening India's democratic institutions over the past 12 years, warning that rebuilding them would take considerable time even after a change in government."Over the last twelve years great damage has been done to the fabric of our country, our democracy and our institutions. Even after this government goes, it will take time to restore our systems back to health and great effort from political parties," she said.However, she expressed confidence that people would support a return to what she described as proper governance."But I am optimistic and I know that the people of India will welcome a return to proper governance," the former Congress chief said.Asked what the Congress could learn from Prime Minister Narendra Modi's political rise, Gandhi said his ideological background was different from that of the Congress but dismissed the need for the party to draw lessons from the RSS."It's true that he comes from a very different ideological world. But there are many ways that people succeed in politics within the Congress party, take for example Dr. Manmohan Singh and Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge. I don't think we have much to learn from the RSS."She also rejected the suggestion that she had ever reconsidered her decision to decline the prime minister's post after the Congress-led alliance won the 2004 general election."No, not at all. That has never crossed my mind. Our experience was by and large a very positive one. We worked as a team, and our roles were distinct, with him (Singh) leading the government and I leading the party."Gandhi's 544-page memoir, "Belonging: A Journey of Love", is scheduled to be released in India by HarperCollins India on November 10. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen has a life that connects two very different places, California and New York. While he spends most of the NFL season in Buffalo, his story began on a family farm in Firebaugh, California. From working in cotton fields as a child to owning a $7.2 million house in Dana Point, Allen’s journey offers an interesting look at his life away from football.Josh Allen was born on May 21, 1996, in Firebaugh, California, a small farming town in the state’s Central Valley, around 40 miles west of Fresno. He grew up there with his parents, Joel and Lavonne Allen, and his three siblings. Long before he became the face of the Buffalo Bills, his everyday life involved helping his family with agricultural work.Farming was not a new business for the Allens. His father, Joel, comes from a long line of farmers, and the family has been connected to the agricultural community for generations. According to a 2021 report by the Los Angeles Times, the extended Allen family owned around 1,200 acres of farmland in the Firebaugh area.The land has played an important role in shaping Josh’s childhood. During summer breaks, he often worked alongside his younger brother instead of spending all his time playing sports.His responsibilities included pulling weeds, digging ditches, moving irrigation pipes and helping with cotton fields.The Los Angeles Times reported that Allen also drove tractors while working on the farm. These were not occasional visits to a family property. He was expected to help with the regular work, just like other members of the family.His childhood in Firebaugh also gave him a close connection to the local community. His father once described the town to the Los Angeles Times by saying, “Our community, it’s a pretty special place. We kind of take care of each other.”That connection has remained important even after Allen moved away to build his football career.The Allen family has continued its farming business even as Josh’s NFL career has grown. Cantaloupes have been one of its main products, with the family also working on expanding its agricultural operation through pistachio farming.In an August 2025 report by The Westside Express, Joel Allen explained that the family had started Allen Family Orchards in 2021. At the time, the operation covered around 600 acres, with plans to add more land and eventually reach 1,000 acres.Pistachios have also become an important part of the family’s plans. The 2025 report explained that the family expected 2026 to be its first major production year for the crop. Josh has also been involved in promoting pistachios through a partnership with Wonderful Pistachios.However, the family’s farming connection is no longer limited to California. In September 2026, Joel and Lavonne brought their agricultural business to Western New York through a partnership with Tops Friendly Markets.According to WGRZ, the JA17 Allen Family Farms cantaloupes returned to participating Tops stores, giving Buffalo residents an opportunity to buy products grown by the quarterback’s family. The family also introduced merchandise, including T-shirts, hats, mugs and tote bags.There was a community reason behind the project as well. A portion of the proceeds from the melon sales and merchandise was set to support the Patricia Allen Fund at Golisano Children’s Hospital of Buffalo.Joel explained that the family wanted to use the partnership to support a community that had welcomed their son. His mother, Lavonne, also described Buffalo as a second home for the family.For Josh Allen, this connection brings together the two places that have played major roles in his life. His family continues to work in California, while their products have found a place among Bills supporters in New York.California may be where Josh Allen grew up, but Buffalo has become his professional home. The quarterback joined the Bills in 2018 after being selected seventh overall in the NFL Draft. Since then, he has made the Buffalo area an important part of his life.Allen owns property in Orchard Park, a suburb of Buffalo where the Bills’ stadium and training facilities are located. According to Realtor.com, he purchased land in the area in 2021 for around $500,000 and later had a custom-built mansion developed there.The property sits on approximately 31 acres, giving Allen plenty of private space away from the attention that comes with being an NFL star. Its location is also convenient for his football commitments, as it is around eight minutes from Highmark Stadium.The Orchard Park estate has several features that make it stand out. Reports describe a large swimming pool, a separate pool house and a private sports court that can be used for basketball and tennis. The property also has a private par-3 golf hole, giving Allen another way to enjoy his time away from football.His connection to Orchard Park goes beyond owning an expensive property. Living close to the Bills’ facilities allows him to remain connected to the team throughout the season without having to travel far for practices and other commitments.According to Mansion Global, Allen also owns two homes in Orchard Park. However, detailed information about the interiors and current arrangements of his private residences has not been publicly confirmed.Unlike his California property, which has been listed for sale, there has been no comparable confirmed announcement that he is selling his Orchard Park estate.Apart from his property in New York, Josh Allen also has a connection to Southern California through his Dana Point house. He purchased the property in 2023 for $7.2 million, according to Mansion Global. The house is located in Monarch Bay, a gated coastal community in Orange County.The property covers approximately 2,808 square feet and has four bedrooms and three bathrooms. Built in 1962, it features a single-level design with mid-century architecture. The house also has large windows and sliding glass doors that connect the indoor living areas to the backyard.The main living space includes a family room with high ceilings, a formal dining area and a kitchen with quartz countertops. The primary bedroom has a separate sitting area, while the backyard offers outdoor space, a hot tub and patio areas.Another attraction is the location. The property is around half a mile from the beach, and residents of Monarch Bay have access to the private Monarch Bay Beach Club.Josh Allen’s plans for the house changed after his purchase. In July 2025, he reportedly put the property on the market for $8.5 million. However, it was taken off the market in January 2026.The quarterback made another attempt to sell it in September 2026, this time with a reduced asking price of $7.95 million. Realtor.com reported the new listing on September 14, while Mansion Global also covered his second attempt to sell the property.The decision to list the Dana Point house does not mean Allen has lost his connection to California. He was born and raised in the state, and his parents and family farming business remain based there.His property choices reflect the different parts of his life. Orchard Park keeps him close to his NFL career, while Dana Point offered a place to enjoy California’s warmer weather during the offseason. Firebaugh, meanwhile, remains the place where his family’s story began.
Article Summary: Josh Allen was born on May 21, 1996, in Firebaugh, California, a small farming town in the state’s Central Valley. His father, Joel, comes from a long line of farmers, and the family has been connected to the agricultural community for generations. The extended Allen family owned around 1,200 acres of farmland in the Firebaugh area. In 2021, Josh Allen bought land in Orchard Park, a suburb of Buffalo where the Bills’ training facilities are located. In September 2026, Joel and Lavonne Allen brought their agricultural business to Western New York.

Article Title: Ryan Clark accuses ESPN of targeting Troy Aikman as Joe Buck secures $108 million deal amid contract dispute

Ryan Clark has accused ESPN of creating a negative image of Troy Aikman as the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback faces an uncertain future with the network. Speaking on The Pivot podcast, Clark said he believes ESPN is allowing negative stories about Aikman to shape public opinion instead of addressing his contract situation directly. Having recently lost his own job at ESPN, Clark says he recognises the pattern.Clark shared his thoughts on the November 6 episode of The Pivot, where he questioned why ESPN had not shown the same public support for Aikman that it had shown other on-air personalities.He began by praising Aikman and his longtime broadcasting partner Joe Buck, who have worked together for 25 years.“But I look at Troy Aikman and Joe Buck. I believe they’re the best booth in football, and for 25 years, they’ve proved that,” Clark said. He also credited the pair for helping ESPN secure better NFL games and its first Super Bowl broadcast.Clark then raised concerns about the stories surrounding Aikman, including reports of tension between the two broadcasters.“Somebody is trying to make Troy Aikman look like the b*****d son,” he said.The former NFL safety believes the network’s handling of the situation is creating an image of Aikman as the problem, even though the full story has not been made public.“You mentioned the leaks. I’ve been around there. I know how it starts to happen when they’re trying to build a narrative about you,” Clark explained.He added that ESPN had previously supported people publicly, even when they made mistakes, but he had not seen the same response in Aikman’s case.“They haven’t done that for Troy,” Clark said. “So I do feel like there is a push to make him the bad guy, whether he is or not.”The contract situation has become more complicated since Buck agreed to a reported six-year, $108 million extension with ESPN in September. Aikman, meanwhile, is approaching the end of his five-year, $90 million agreement, signed in 2022. According to Front Office Sports, ESPN has not made him a formal offer, while his representatives reportedly proposed a return with a raise similar to Buck’s.ESPN has said it will not discuss talent contracts publicly before the Super Bowl.Clark’s criticism also comes from his own experience with ESPN. The network ended its relationship with him on July 20 after 11 years, informing him about the decision while he was appearing on NFL Live.According to The Athletic, ESPN had initially planned to tell Clark the following morning but changed its plans because executives were concerned that news of his departure might leak.Clark believes the way his exit was handled helps him understand what Aikman could be facing now.“I know that they have ways of maneuvering to protect people, and I know that they have ways of putting people in positions where a narrative is built around them, so when they make their exit, they can seem like the good guys. Because I was a part of that. This is what this feels like to me,” he said.Meanwhile, Aikman has already spoken about his uncertain future. During an appearance on Dallas radio station 96.7 The Ticket, he said he planned to finish the season before becoming a free agent.He also admitted that there was a 50-50 chance he would not return to television next season.Despite the uncertainty, Aikman and Buck are expected to work together through Super Bowl LXI on February 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium. Whether they continue as ESPN’s Monday Night Football broadcasting team after that remains unclear.
Article Summary: Ryan Clark accuses ESPN of targeting Troy Aikman as Joe Buck secures $108 million deal amid contract dispute. The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback faces an uncertain future with the network. Clark believes ESPN is allowing negative stories to shape public opinion instead of addressing his contract situation.

Boris Becker was once the very definition of tennis excellence, and the German was the youngest male to win the Wimbledon singles title in 1985, at just 17, beginning a career that would ultimately yield him six Grand Slam singles championships and worldwide fame. His success made him one of Germany’s most celebrated sporting figures.However, the years following his retirement in 1999 brought a very different set of headlines. Financial difficulties, personal controversies, a bankruptcy declaration in the United Kingdom and a prison sentence gradually overshadowed parts of his sporting legacy. Becker's story was an illustration of how a remarkable playing career does not necessarily translate into financial security or shield a public reputation from legal woes.Since the end of his playing career, Becker’s public image has changed dramatically. His achievements continued to be respected throughout the tennis world, but the focus increasingly shifted to his personal relationships, financial choices and legal disputes. His later work as a commentator and coach provided a way back into the sport, but the bankruptcy proceedings and the criminal case brought renewed scrutiny.Becker announced himself to the world at Wimbledon in 1985, defeating Kevin Curren in the final to win the championship aged 17. He became the first unseeded player to win the men's singles title at the tournament and quickly developed into an international sporting sensation.His success continued beyond that breakthrough. Becker won three Wimbledon titles, two Australian Open championships and one US Open singles title. He also became the world No. 1, winning 49 singles titles in his professional career.After his retirement in 1999, Becker stayed involved in the sport through TV commentary and coaching. He has been particularly successful with Novak Djokovic during the 2014-16 period, when the Serb won six Grand Slam titles. Becker also became a familiar face and voice on tennis broadcasting, including for the BBC. These roles helped maintain his sporting relevance even as his private life attracted media attention.Becker’s financial difficulties became a major public issue after his retirement. During his 2022 trial, he told the court that his career earnings of approximately $50 million had been reduced by divorce costs, child maintenance payments and expensive lifestyle commitments. He also said he took a sharp drop in income after leaving professional tennis.His debts included property-related borrowing and other obligations. The financial strain that led to bankruptcy reportedly came from a loan from private bank Arbuthnot Latham and more borrowing, according to testimony during the trial. His defense also pointed to his reliance on financial advisers and difficulties managing his money.On June 21, 2017, Becker was declared bankrupt by a London court after failing to repay a substantial loan connected to his property in Mallorca, Spain. His finances were examined in the bankruptcy proceedings and he had to disclose assets and financial transactions to the appointed trustees.The case also included items related to his tennis career. His collection was auctioned in 2019 to raise money for creditors. The auction included significant sporting items, reflecting how his financial situation had reached beyond ordinary personal expenses and into his professional legacy.The scale of his liabilities became another subject of public discussion. Reports during the proceedings described debts approaching £50 million. Becker disputed some claims about his financial position, but the bankruptcy case continued and eventually led to criminal proceedings over the disclosure of assets and transactions.Becker’s legal difficulties predated his 2017 bankruptcy. In 2002, he was convicted in Germany of tax evasion and attempted tax evasion, receiving a two-year suspended prison sentence and a financial penalty. The case became an early indication of the challenges that would later affect his public image.The most serious consequences followed the UK bankruptcy proceedings. Becker was convicted by a jury at Southwark Crown Court in April 2022 of four counts under the Insolvency Act. The charges included concealing debt, removing property and failing to disclose assets and financial information required during the bankruptcy process.The trial also heard of claims of precious items, including trophies from Wimbledon. But Becker was acquitted of several charges, including claims that he failed to hand over his trophies and medals. It is important to separate those allegations from the four offenses he was in fact convicted of.Becker was convicted on April 29, 2022, and sentenced to two years and six months in prison. The court's decision marked a dramatic change in the public story of a player who had once been celebrated for his achievements at the All England Club.Becker served eight months of his sentence before being released in December 2022 under an early-release arrangement for foreign nationals. He was subsequently deported from the United Kingdom to Germany. The experience brought another major change to his professional life, particularly because he had spent years working in British tennis broadcasting and living in London.2024 was also a critical year in his bankruptcy process. He was discharged from bankruptcy by a UK court after agreeing a settlement with the trustees. The decision came after the finalizing of arrangements for a significant payment and the outstanding obligations in his case.His comments showed how the consequences of the case continued to affect his relationship with the country and the tournament that had defined his sporting career.Becker’s legacy now carries two contrasting chapters. His achievements as a six-time Grand Slam singles champion remain an important part of tennis history, while his bankruptcy and insolvency convictions have become equally prominent in accounts of his life after retirement.His role as commentator and coach showed he could be a force in tennis beyond his playing days. But the legal proceedings altered the nature of the telling of his story after his career, making it less about sporting success and more about fiscal responsibility and personal accountability.
Article Summary: Boris Becker was the youngest male to win the Wimbledon singles title in 1985, at just 17. His success made him one of Germany’s most celebrated sporting figures. But the years following his retirement in 1999 brought a very different set of headlines. Financial difficulties, personal controversies, a bankruptcy declaration in the United Kingdom and a prison sentence gradually overshadowed parts of his sporting legacy.

Article Title: 'Always found her way to the finish line': Family releases obituary for NYC Marathon runner Rachel Apa who died from rhabdomyolysis
Article Text:
Family releases heartbreaking obituary for Rachel Apa who died during marathon in NYC.

The family of Rachel Apa, the 24-year-old runner who died after collapsing just two miles short of the finish line at the New York City Marathon, has released a moving obituary remembering her as a determined athlete who "always found her way to the finish line".Apa, from Lewisberry, Pennsylvania, collapsed near Mile 24 of the marathon in Central Park on November 1. She was taken to Mount Sinai Hospital but died hours later. Her family said she suffered from rhabdomyolysis, a rare condition involving the breakdown of muscle tissue."With determination, discipline, and a heart fully committed to whatever she pursued, she always found her way to the finish line," her family wrote in the obituary.Recalling her final moments during the race, the family wrote that Apa had completed 24 miles at an incredible pace, with a wide grin on her face."On Sunday, November 1, 2026, after running 24 miles at an incredible pace and with a grin that stretched ear to ear, the only thing strong enough to physically stop her body met Rachel on 85th Street," the obituary said."Her spirit was so powerful and full of vitality that not even her body could contain it," the family added.The obituary described Apa as strong-willed and someone who naturally took charge. Despite being just 24, she had already achieved several milestones and inspired pride among those who knew her."At just 24, Rachel had already accomplished so much and given those who knew her countless reasons to be proud. She moved through the world with purpose, always setting high expectations for herself," her family wrote.Beyond athletics, Apa was passionate about animals, particularly her dogs, whom her family described as her "forever children". She was also a talented baker who had created a cookie recipe so irresistible that her family joked they had to get rid of it for the sake of their health."She created a cookie recipe so perfect it had to be thrown away for the sake of our health," the obituary read.Apa was a former Division I field hockey player at Bucknell University. She graduated from the university in 2024 and had been pursuing a master's degree in business administration at Charleston Southern University while working.She was running her first New York City Marathon to raise money for Parkinson's disease research in honour of her grandfather, who died of the disease in 2022.In a LinkedIn post before the race, Apa had credited her grandfather with teaching her to remain active, push her limits and embrace challenges."My grandfather was one of my role models growing up. He taught me to stay active, push my limits, and embrace challenges," she had written.Her father, Steve Apa, had earlier said his daughter was in excellent health and had trained for the marathon. He had been exchanging text messages with her throughout the race, but communication stopped when she reached Mile 24.According to her family, doctors told them that she died from rhabdomyolysis, a potentially life-threatening condition in which damaged muscle tissue releases substances into the bloodstream that can cause kidney damage and other complications.New York Road Runners, which organizes the marathon, said a bystander administered CPR after Apa collapsed. Event medical staff also performed CPR and used a defibrillator before paramedics took her to hospital.The New York City medical examiner's office had said it was investigating her death.
Article Summary: Rachel Apa collapsed near Mile 24 of the marathon in Central Park on November 1. Her family said she suffered from rhabdomyolysis, a rare condition involving the breakdown of muscle tissue. She was running her first New York City Marathon to raise money for Parkinson's disease research in honour of her grandfather.

Article Title: Brittany Mahomes, Kelly Stafford face Linda Cohn's blunt reality check over controversial NFL complaints
Article Text:
Brittany Mahomes, Kelly Stafford face Linda Cohn's blunt reality check over controversial NFL complaints

Brittany Mahomes questions officials after Kansas City Chiefs lose to Denver Broncos

Kelly Stafford's complaint about the Los Angeles Rams schedule also draws Linda Cohn's attention

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Brittany Mahomes and Kelly Stafford have faced criticism after speaking out against the NFL over officiating and scheduling issues. Now, former ESPN SportsCenter anchor Linda Cohn has questioned how both women chose to share their complaints. Cohn said that being married to an NFL quarterback does not stop them from having opinions, but it also does not protect them from criticism. She had a simple message for the two women: “Know the room.” Her comments come after both wives received negative reactions from football fans on social media.The incident happened during Kansas City's 28-24 defeat to the Denver Broncos on November 1. With only seconds left, Patrick Mahomes connected with Rashee Rice for what appeared to be a winning touchdown. However, officials called a false start on Chiefs right tackle Jaylon Moore. The penalty wiped out the score and pushed Kansas City back five yards. Denver then stopped the Chiefs on the final play to secure the win.Brittany did not hide her frustration with the decision. She questioned why officials would make such a call on a potential game-winning touchdown and suggested the Chiefs were being treated differently.She wrote on Instagram: “You can't tell me you call that on a game-winning TD, oh wait yeah I can cause it's us.”She followed that message with another comment: “That was the weakest call I have ever seen.”Her reaction also drew attention because the Chiefs had suffered their second straight defeat. However, the discussion soon moved beyond the penalty itself, with fans questioning her suggestion that the team was being unfairly treated.Kelly Stafford had raised a different concern just days earlier. Matthew Stafford's wife questioned the NFL's decision to give the Los Angeles Rams a shorter break before their Thanksgiving Eve game against the Green Bay Packers on November 25.The Rams are scheduled to face the Arizona Cardinals on November 15 before hosting Green Bay 10 days later. Kelly questioned the decision and wrote on her Instagram Story:“Just curious to hear the thought process behind making the Rams the only team in the NFL without a true bye week.”She also explained why she felt the schedule was tiring, even for someone who watches from the stands.“Because after 18 years around this league, even I need a week off during the season… and I have never played a single snap. I'm tired just watching from the stands. Can't imagine how the guys feel.”Her main concern was the time players get to recover between games. However, there is one detail worth noting: the Packers also have the same 10-day gap before their November 25 meeting with the Rams. So, Los Angeles is not the only team facing that shorter break.Linda Cohn understood Kelly's concern about player recovery but felt her personal comment about being tired from watching games could be difficult for ordinary fans to relate to.Cohn explained that NFL players face physical demands and need enough time to recover. However, she also asked Kelly to consider people who work long hours, look after their families and deal with everyday expenses before sitting down to watch football.Speaking about both women, Cohn said: “Marriage to a quarterback doesn't disqualify you from commentary, from having an opinion. It also doesn't exempt your commentary from criticism. Kelly and Brittany are two people making public statements.”She then shared the message that became the main point of her criticism:“Sometimes before you hit post, the most useful question is, how is this going to sound to somebody whose life looks very, very different from my own? Three words, know the room.”Cohn also made it clear that Kelly had raised an important issue about player recovery. She said: “Kelly makes the case for player recovery that's a conversation worth having. Just understand why your own game day exhaustion might not generate the sympathy you expect.”For Cohn, the issue was not whether Brittany and Kelly had the right to speak. It was how their words might sound to people who experience football and everyday life very differently.
Article Summary: Brittany Mahomes questioned officials after Kansas City Chiefs lose to Denver Broncos. Kelly Stafford's complaint about the Los Angeles Rams schedule also draws Linda Cohn's attention. Cohn said that being married to an NFL quarterback does not stop them from having opinions, but it does not protect them from criticism.

Article Title: Camille Kostek reacts to Rob Gronkowski’s political controversy after former Patriots star faces New Hampshire speculation
Article Text:
Camille Kostek has backed Rob Gronkowski after the former New England Patriots star denied claims that the couple supported Turning Point USA during their Election Day visit to New Hampshire. (Getty Images)

Camille Kostek backs Rob Gronkowski after political speculation

Gronkowski explains what happened in New Hampshire

Rob Gronkowski has rejected claims that he and Camille Kostek were supporting Turning Point USA during their Election Day visit to New Hampshire. The former New England Patriots tight end said the speculation was “upsetting and eye opening” after photos of the couple near a tent bearing the conservative group's logo began circulating online. Kostek, meanwhile, reposted Gronkowski's statement on Instagram, signaling her support for his response. The couple said they were simply greeting fans and taking pictures, not campaigning for a political organization.Gronkowski's statement came two days after the couple's appearance at polling locations in New Hampshire on November 3. The former NFL star and Kostek greeted fans, signed jerseys and posed for photos. Some of those interactions took place near a tent displaying the Turning Point USA logo, which led to questions about their political leanings.However, a spokesperson for Turning Point USA told CBS News that Gronkowski was not part of the organization's group. The spokesperson said the former tight end had walked past the tent.That distinction became central to Gronkowski's response. He wanted to make it clear that being photographed near the group did not mean he supported its political work.“It has been upsetting and eye opening to see the narratives around my visit to NH on Election Day with Camille,” Gronkowski said on Instagram on November 5.He then addressed the speculation directly.“In regard to the images and videos circulating we are not endorsed by or affiliated with Turning Point USA.”Kostek reposted his statement to her Instagram Story later that day. Her response was brief, but it showed that she stood behind Gronkowski as the couple tried to clear up the confusion.The incident also highlights how a few images can quickly shape public perception. A photo taken during an ordinary interaction may tell only part of the story, especially when it involves a public figure and a politically active organization.Gronkowski offered more detail about the visit, saying the couple had stopped at Goffstown High School before crossing the street to meet fans.“After stopping at Goffstown high school we crossed the street to greet excited fans yelling out our names before leaving to the next location. We simply took some pictures and I signed some things for them before leaving.”He also stressed that the couple had interacted with people from different political backgrounds that morning.The former Patriots star said they “took photos with people across the political spectrum throughout that morning” and added, “We cannot control what the media has made of it and running with — so we are here to shut down the false narratives.”Gronkowski was particularly unhappy with how the images had been presented. He called it “disappointing to see an innocent moment stripped of context and turned into clickbait.”He ended his message with a broader appeal, saying, “Our message has always been and always will be to treat everyone with kindness and hope you all will do the same.”New Hampshire voters were deciding two major races on Election Day, including a vacant U.S. Senate seat and the governor's race. Republican Gov. Kelly Ayotte narrowly defeated Democrat Cinde Warmington, while Chris Pappas defeated John Sununu to become the first openly gay man elected to the U.S. Senate.Against that political backdrop, Gronkowski and Kostek's appearance drew attention they say they never intended to attract. Their statement makes one thing clear: the couple wants their interactions with fans to remain separate from political endorsements.
Article Summary: Rob Gronkowski and Camille Kostek were photographed near a Turning Point USA tent during their Election Day visit to New Hampshire. The former New England Patriots tight end said the speculation was “upsetting and eye opening” The couple said they were simply greeting fans and taking pictures, not campaigning for a political organization.

Article Title: Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and his wife, Ann Michael, gave more than $25,000 worth of helmets, shoulder pads and footballs to Chelsea High School in Massachusetts
Article Text:
Drake Maye and his wife, Ann Michael, donated more than $25,000 in sports gear to Chelsea High School. Image Credits: @drake.maye/Instagram

A gift with a bigger goal

The Mayes’ donation to Chelsea High School marks the launch of Power Up Play, a program for high school sports across New England. Image Credits: @annmichaelhmaye/Instagram

Why gear can be a barrier

Why the teacher gift matters

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Imagine wanting to play football but not having the gear to do it. That's the reality for many students around the world. Cost can be one of the many hurdles in their way. New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and his wife, Ann Michael, donated more than $25,000 worth of helmets, shoulder pads, and footballs to Chelsea High School in Massachusetts on October 28, 2026. According to The Patriot Ledger, the donation was made through the MayeDay Family Foundation and Good Sports, a Boston-based nonprofit. The gift also launched something more. It marks the start of a new programme that aims to help high school athletes across New England.The initiative is called the Power Up Play. It's a collaboration between the foundation and Good Sports to support after-school sports programmes at high schools in New England. The aim of this programme, according to the press release, extends beyond just providing sports equipment. It also hopes to help young athletes build confidence, resilience, and life skills that carry over in school and everyday life. The MayeDay Family Foundation is relatively new. It was founded by Drake and Ann in March 2026 for children and families in need. The foundation intends to fund programmes in New England, including Boston Children's Hospital, as well as in the couple's home state of North Carolina.It has been swift in its actions. In May, it organised its first event, a celebrity softball game in Polar Park, Worcester, Massachusetts, that raised over $500,000. In September, the Mayes donated $15,000 to fulfil the Amazon wish list of all teachers and support specialists at Alfred Lima Sr. Elementary School in Providence, Rhode Island.Joining a team is often more expensive than people expect. The C.S. Mott Children’s Hospital National Poll on Children’s Health , based at the University of Michigan, surveyed 961 parents who answered questions about 1,323 children in middle or high school. Its report from 2019 found the average cost of school sports, including fees, equipment, and travel, was $408. It was much more than arts, which was $251 and clubs or other activities, which was $126. The poll also found a gap by income. Students from households earning less than $100,000 a year did not participate in any school activities at twice the rate of students from higher-income families. Overall, 18% of students were not participating in any extracurricular activity. Many parents were not accessing help either. Only 7% had ever applied for a fee waiver or scholarship, and 19% said they didn't know how to. The poll is from 2019, so the costs might be different today.The Mayes’ help didn't stop at sports. Their September gift was for the teachers, and national data shows why that's important. A report from the National Center for Education Statistics , a part of the US Department of Education, examined how much public school teachers spend on classroom supplies without being reimbursed. In the 2014-15 school year, teachers spending their own money spent an average of $478 and a median of $297. Teachers of elementary grades spent an average of $525. In schools where 75% or more of the students are eligible for free or reduced-price lunch, teachers spend an average of $550 compared to the $434 in schools with 0-34% eligibility.These numbers are from a survey back in 2015-16; today’s numbers might be different. Still, they show why fulfilling teachers’ wish lists can matter.One gift will probably not break down all the barriers. Transportation and having a job were also cited in the Michigan poll as reasons students sit out, particularly among boys. It's too early to see how far Power Up Play will go, but the concept is easy to relate to. For some students, a helmet and a set of pads can be a little door to a much bigger world.
Article Summary: New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and his wife, Ann Michael, donated more than $25,000 worth of helmets, shoulder pads, and footballs to Chelsea High School. The gift marks the start of a new programme that aims to help high school athletes across New England. In September, the Mayes donated $15,000 to fulfil the Amazon wish list of all teachers and support specialists at Alfred Lima Sr. Elementary School in Rhode Island.
